main_text.l: Et omne sicinum solum, misero, precor,
Concede patri ne sit ipse carnifex,
Hunc cadat alter quem soles, lubens feram.
Non dicta mutabunt Superi, tua cadet
O, quum reuerti me mea solum siderit,
Quid dicet sxor? quum perisse filium
Fletus acerbos fundet? O, tantos quibus
Verbis dolores leniam? Si te, Deus,
Si nemo tuis factam auspiciis illam putet,
Mox mox per srbes cursibus solans citis
Diras ꝯ omnis impre cata gens truces
Quis pollicenti tibi bona plura credet,
Quis nomen inuocare post tuum solet,
Promissa si præstare temnis? ꝯ suos

page.notes: Printed text is in a 16th–17th century Latin verse drama; some letters (s for long s and s/f forms) are uncertain; the words "Diras ꝯ omnis impre cata" and "Quis pollicenti" are read with doubt; marks ꝯ are printed ampersand-like signs. The bottom line reads partly as a catchword-like mark "V" and a small mark "ꝯ"; the final word "sanguisimi" is cut at the page edge and may be read as [?].
